doc_summary: The Wireshark Foundation released version 4.6.3 on January 14, 2026, addressing four critical security vulnerabilities and multiple stability issues. The update targets crashes and infinite loop conditions affecting the network protocol analysis tool. The release patches vulnerabilities identified between versions 4.6.0 and 4.6.2, and the 4.4.x branch. The BLF file parser vulnerability (wnpa-sec-2026-01) could trigger crashes with malformed packet trace files. OSS-Fuzz discovered the IEEE 802.11 dissector crash (wnpa-sec-2026-02), posing exploitation risks through malicious packet injection. Fatih Çelik identified a crash in the SOME/IP-SD dissector (wnpa-sec-2026-03), affecting automotive Ethernet communications. Tom Needham discovered the HTTP3 dissector vulnerability (wnpa-sec-2026-04), causing an infinite loop during traffic decryption. Beyond security patches, version 4.6.3 resolves nine functional bugs impacting platform compatibility and protocol dissection accuracy. Organizations using Wireshark for network troubleshooting, security analysis, or protocol development should prioritize upgrading to version 4.6.3 or the parallel 4.4.13 release.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves exploitation of vulnerabilities in Wireshark dissectors, specifically targeting the BLF file parser, IEEE 802.11, SOME/IP-SD, and HTTP3 dissectors. The exploitation stage is critical, with no significant activity detected in other stages.

Title: NVIDIA GPU Display Drivers Vulnerabilities

Victim.Description: Users of NVIDIA GPU Display Drivers on Windows, Linux, and virtualization platforms.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in NVIDIA GPU Display Drivers, affecting Windows, Linux, and virtualization platforms. The adversary could exploit these vulnerabilities to execute malicious code and escalate privileges. The capabilities include exploiting memory safety and integer overflow issues. The infrastructure details are not specified, but the victims are users of NVIDIA drivers across various platforms.
doc_summary: NVIDIA has released critical security updates for its GPU Display Drivers after discovering multiple high-severity vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute malicious code and escalate privileges on affected systems. The security bulletin, published on January 27, 2026, addresses five distinct vulnerabilities affecting Windows, Linux, and virtualization platforms, with CVSS scores reaching 7.8. The most significant vulnerabilities involve memory safety issues in NVIDIA’s driver software across multiple platforms. CVE-2025-33217 affects the Windows Display Driver and stems from a use-after-free condition that attackers can exploit to achieve code execution, privilege escalation, data tampering, denial of service, and information disclosure. Two additional flaws, CVE-2025-33218 and CVE-2025-33219, involve integer overflow vulnerabilities in the Windows kernel mode layer (nvlddmkm.sys) and Linux kernel module respectively, presenting identical attack vectors and impacts. The vulnerabilities require local access with low-level privileges to exploit, but successful attacks grant attackers high-level control over confidentiality, integrity, and availability of affected systems. All three flaws carry identical CVSS v3.1 base scores of 7.8 and are classified as high severity. The NVIDIA vGPU software also contains a similar use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2025-33220) in the Virtual GPU Manager, where malicious guests could trigger heap memory access after memory deallocation. NVIDIA has released updated drivers across four major branches (R590, R580, R570, and R535) for GeForce, NVIDIA RTX, Quadro, NVS, and Tesla products. Windows users should upgrade to driver versions 591.59, 582.16, 573.76, or 539.64 depending on their branch. Linux users need to install versions 590.48.01, 580.126.09, 570.211.01, or 535.288.01. Additionally, a medium-severity vulnerability (CVE-2025-33237) in the NVIDIA HD Audio Driver could cause denial-of-service through NULL pointer dereference exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves the exploitation stage, where adversaries can exploit vulnerabilities in NVIDIA drivers to execute malicious code and escalate privileges. The vulnerabilities require local access with low-level privileges, but successful exploitation grants high-level control over affected systems. The remediation involves applying NVIDIA's security updates and implementing least privilege access controls.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes vulnerabilities as the primary indicators. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified. The focus is on the exploitation of memory safety and integer overflow vulnerabilities in NVIDIA drivers. The remediation involves applying security updates and monitoring for unusual driver behavior.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new campaign by the China-linked threat actor UAT-8099, targeting vulnerable Internet Information Services (IIS) servers across Asia, with a focus on Thailand and Vietnam. The campaign, discovered by Cisco Talos, involves the use of web shells, PowerShell scripts, and the GotoHTTP tool to gain remote access to compromised servers. UAT-8099, first documented in October 2025, exploits IIS servers in multiple countries, including India, Thailand, Vietnam, Canada, and Brazil, for search engine optimization (SEO) fraud using the BadIIS malware. The campaign shares similarities with the WEBJACK campaign, based on tool and infrastructure overlaps. The threat actor employs SoftEther VPN and EasyTier for control, and has evolved its strategy to evade detection and maintain persistence. The BadIIS malware has two new variants, IISHijack and asdSearchEngine, targeting specific regions. The campaign's end goal is to redirect search engine crawlers to SEO fraud sites while injecting malicious JavaScript into responses for regular users.
kill_chain_summary: The UAT-8099 campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable IIS servers, followed by weaponization of exploits. Delivery is achieved through web shells and PowerShell scripts, leading to exploitation of IIS vulnerabilities. Installation of BadIIS malware ensures persistence, while command and control is maintained via GotoHTTP. The final objective is SEO fraud, redirecting search engine crawlers.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a high-severity vulnerability in OpenSSL, identified as CVE-2025-15467, which allows remote code execution through a stack buffer overflow in CMS AuthEnvelopedData parsing. The vulnerability affects OpenSSL versions 3.0 to 3.6, with a fix available in subsequent patched versions. The flaw was reported by Stanislav Fort from Aisle Research, and the patch was developed by Igor Ustinov. Organizations using OpenSSL for secure communications, particularly those implementing S/MIME email encryption, are at risk and should prioritize upgrading to the patched versions to mitigate potential exploitation.
doc_summary: The OpenSSL Project disclosed a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2025-15467, affecting versions 3.0 through 3.6 of the cryptography library. This flaw, a stack buffer overflow in CMS AuthEnvelopedData parsing, allows potential remote code execution by processing maliciously crafted AEAD parameters. The vulnerability impacts the handling of the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) AuthEnvelopedData structure, particularly when using AEAD ciphers like AES-GCM. The issue arises from copying an oversized Initialization Vector into a fixed-size stack buffer without bounds checking, leading to a stack-based out-of-bounds write operation. This attack vector is concerning as it occurs before authentication checks, negating the need for valid key material. Affected systems include those parsing untrusted CMS or PKCS#7 content, such as S/MIME AuthEnvelopedData implementations. OpenSSL versions 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 are unaffected. The vulnerability was reported by Stanislav Fort from Aisle Research, with a fix by Igor Ustinov. Users should upgrade to patched versions to mitigate risks.

doc_summary: Google has released a new Chrome Stable Channel update for desktop, addressing a high-severity vulnerability in the Background Fetch API that could expose users to security risks. The latest Chrome version, 144.0.7559.109/.110 for Windows and macOS and 144.0.7559.109 for Linux, is now rolling out to users. The patched vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-1504, is described as an inappropriate implementation in Background Fetch API and is rated High severity. The issue was reported by security researcher Luan Herrera on January 9, 2026, and Google awarded a $3,000 bug bounty for the discovery. The Background Fetch API allows websites to download large files in the background, even if the browser tab is closed. An implementation flaw in this component could potentially be abused to bypass security boundaries, mishandle permissions, or process background requests in unsafe ways. Google is withholding the full bug report and exploit details until a majority of Chrome users have updated, reducing the risk of active exploitation by threat actors. Google credits tools such as AddressSanitizer, MemorySanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, Control Flow Integrity, libFuzzer, and AFL for helping detect many security issues earlier in the development cycle.

doc_summary: TA584, a prolific initial access broker, has been using Tsundere Bot and XWorm remote access trojan to gain network access, potentially leading to ransomware attacks. Proofpoint researchers have tracked TA584 since 2020, noting a significant increase in operations in 2025. Tsundere Bot, linked to a Russian-speaking operator, is used for information gathering, data exfiltration, lateral movement, and installing additional payloads. TA584's activity tripled in late 2025, expanding targets beyond North America and the UK/Ireland to Germany, various European countries, and Australia. The attack chain involves emails from compromised accounts via SendGrid and Amazon SES, leading to a CAPTCHA and ClickFix page, executing a PowerShell command to load XWorm or Tsundere Bot. Tsundere Bot, a malware-as-a-service platform, uses Node.js, retrieves C2 addresses from the Ethereum blockchain, and communicates over WebSockets. It profiles infected machines, executes JavaScript from C2, and uses infected hosts as SOCKS proxies. TA584 is expected to broaden its target range and experiment with various payloads.

Delivery is executed via phishing emails with unique URLs. Exploitation occurs when targets execute a PowerShell command, leading to the installation of malware. Command and control is maintained through WebSocket communication with C2 servers. Actions on objectives include data exfiltration and lateral movement, facilitated by Tsundere Bot's capabilities.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a malicious Visual Studio Code extension named 'ClawdBot Agent - AI Coding Assistant' that exploited the popularity of the Moltbot AI assistant. The extension, published by 'clawdbot', was designed to drop a payload on compromised hosts, retrieving a 'config.json' file from 'clawdbot.getintwopc.site' to execute a binary 'Code.exe' deploying ConnectWise ScreenConnect. The extension connected to 'meeting.bulletmailer.net:8041', granting attackers persistent remote access. It included fallback mechanisms using Dropbox and 'darkgptprivate.com'. The incident exposed Moltbot instances, revealing configuration data and credentials. Researchers highlighted architectural issues in Clawdbot, emphasizing the need for secure configurations.

Exploitation occurs when the extension executes the payload, leading to installation of a remote access tool. Command and control is established through a C2 server, enabling actions on objectives such as data exfiltration and user impersonation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves remote unauthenticated threat actors exploiting critical vulnerabilities in SolarWinds Web Help Desk software. The infrastructure targeted includes Web Help Desk servers used by various sectors globally. Victims are advised to apply patches immediately to mitigate the risk.
doc_summary: SolarWinds has released security updates to patch critical authentication bypass and remote command execution vulnerabilities in its Web Help Desk IT help desk software. The authentication bypass security flaws were reported by watchTowr's Piotr Bazydlo and can be exploited by remote unauthenticated threat actors in low-complexity attacks. Bazydlo also found and reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw stemming from an untrusted data deserialization weakness that can enable attackers without privileges to run commands on vulnerable hosts. A second RCE vulnerability reported by another researcher can also enable unauthenticated attackers to execute commands remotely. SolarWinds also patched a high-severity hardcoded credentials vulnerability discovered by Sebree that, under unspecified circumstances, could grant threat actors with low privileges unauthorized access to administrative functions. The company recommends upgrading vulnerable servers to Web Help Desk 2026.1, which addresses these security flaws. Admins are advised to patch their devices as soon as possible, as hackers have frequently exploited Web Help Desk security vulnerabilities in attacks. In September, SolarWinds addressed CVE-2025-26399, which CISA had noted in attacks more than a year earlier, adding it to its catalog of exploited security bugs and ordering federal agencies to secure their systems within three weeks. At the time, SolarWinds said that the vulnerability was a patch bypass of CVE-2024-28988, which in turn is a patch bypass of CVE-2024-28986. CISA also noted it as actively exploited in October 2024, again asking government agencies to patch their devices. Web Help Desk is widely used by large corporations, healthcare organizations, educational institutions, and government agencies for help desk management. SolarWinds says that its IT management products are used by more than 300,000 customers worldwide.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in SolarWinds Web Help Desk software, allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain initial access through authentication bypass and remote code execution. The exploitation stage is critical, with attackers leveraging these vulnerabilities to execute commands on vulnerable systems. Immediate patching and upgrading to the latest software version are recommended to prevent further exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes vulnerabilities as the primary indicators. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The focus is on the exploitation of known vulnerabilities, which are challenging to change once patched. Organizations must prioritize patch management to mitigate these risks effectively.

doc_summary: Two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-1470 and CVE-2026-0863, were discovered in the n8n workflow automation platform by JFrog researchers. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to fully compromise affected instances, access sensitive data, and execute arbitrary code. Despite requiring authentication, CVE-2026-1470 received a critical severity score of 9.9 due to the potential for arbitrary code execution in n8n’s main node. The vulnerabilities highlight the challenges of safely sandboxing dynamic languages like JavaScript and Python. Exploiting CVE-2026-1470 requires permissions to create or modify a workflow, allowing non-admin users to pivot to infrastructure-level control. The flaws were fixed in n8n versions 1.123.17, 2.4.5, and 2.5.1 for CVE-2026-1470, and in versions 1.123.14, 2.3.5, 2.4.2 for CVE-2026-0863. Users are advised to upgrade to the latest versions. The n8n cloud platform has addressed the issues, affecting only self-hosted versions running a vulnerable release.

diamond_model_summary: The attack on the Polish power grid by ELECTRUM demonstrates a sophisticated adversary with a clear division of roles between KAMACITE and ELECTRUM. doc_summary: In December 2025, a coordinated cyber attack targeted the Polish power grid, attributed to the Russian state-sponsored hacking group ELECTRUM. The attack, described by Dragos, affected communication and control systems at combined heat and power facilities and renewable energy systems. ELECTRUM, linked to Sandworm and KAMACITE, breached Remote Terminal Units and communication infrastructure using exposed network devices and vulnerabilities. The attack did not cause power outages but disabled key equipment beyond repair. KAMACITE's role involved initial access through spear-phishing and exploitation, while ELECTRUM executed operations bridging IT and OT environments, deploying ICS-specific malware. The attack was opportunistic, aiming to inflict damage by wiping Windows-based devices and resetting configurations. The incident highlights the threat to distributed generation systems and the adversaries' deep understanding of electrical grid infrastructure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance by KAMACITE through scanning activities. Initial access was achieved via spear-phishing and exploitation of exposed services. ELECTRUM then installed ICS-specific malware, bridging IT and OT environments. doc_summary: Threat actors with ties to China, specifically Mustang Panda, have been observed using an updated version of the COOLCLIENT backdoor in cyber espionage attacks in 2025. These attacks targeted government entities in Myanmar, Mongolia, Malaysia, and Russia. Kaspersky disclosed details of the updated malware, which is deployed as a secondary backdoor alongside PlugX and LuminousMoth infections. COOLCLIENT is delivered with encrypted loader files and relies on DLL side-loading for execution. Between 2021 and 2025, Mustang Panda leveraged signed binaries from various software products for this purpose. Campaigns in 2024 and 2025 abused software developed by Sangfor, targeting Pakistan and Myanmar. COOLCLIENT was first documented by Sophos in 2022, and Trend Micro attributed it to Mustang Panda, highlighting its capabilities for data theft and surveillance. The malware has been used in long-running espionage campaigns targeting telecom operators. Mustang Panda also deployed stealer programs to extract credentials from browsers and used TONESHELL malware for persistence and payload delivery.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves multiple threat actors, including nation-state adversaries from Russia and China, exploiting a critical vulnerability in WinRAR (CVE-2025-8088) to deliver malware. The infrastructure includes the use of alternate data streams to conceal malicious files. doc_summary: Google revealed that multiple threat actors, including nation-state adversaries from Russia and China, as well as financially motivated groups, are exploiting a critical security flaw in WinRAR (CVE-2025-8088) to establish initial access and deploy various payloads. The vulnerability, a path traversal flaw, allows files to be dropped into the Windows Startup folder for persistence. ESET discovered the flaw being exploited by the RomCom group to deliver SnipBot malware. Google tracks the threat cluster deploying Cuba Ransomware as UNC2596. The flaw has been widely exploited, with attack chains using alternate data streams to conceal malicious files. A China-based actor used the flaw to deliver Poison Ivy. Financially motivated actors deployed RATs and information stealers. The underground economy has seen WinRAR exploits advertised for thousands of dollars, with suppliers like 'zeroplayer' marketing exploits. Another WinRAR vulnerability (CVE-2025-6218) has also been exploited by groups like GOFFEE and Gamaredon.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with the weaponization of malicious archive files exploiting CVE-2025-8088. Installation is achieved by placing malware in the Windows Startup folder for persistence. Command and control are established using RATs, allowing attackers to execute actions on objectives such as data theft. The incident highlights the importance of patching vulnerabilities and monitoring for suspicious file activities.

Victim.Description: Users of the PyPI repository who downloaded the malicious packages.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a threat actor using malicious PyPI packages to deliver a Python RAT. The adversary's capability includes obfuscation and slopsquatting techniques, with infrastructure involving a domain and IP address for C2. Victims are users of PyPI who downloaded the packages, with a medium impact severity.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified two malicious packages in the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository, named spellcheckerpy and spellcheckpy, which masquerade as spellcheckers but deliver a remote access trojan (RAT). These packages were downloaded over 1,000 times before removal. The attack involved a base64-encoded payload hidden in a Basque language dictionary file, which downloads a Python RAT from the domain updatenet.work, associated with IP 172.86.73.139 managed by RouterHosting LLC. The attack timeline includes the release of spellcheckpy version 1.2.0 on January 21, 2026, which enabled payload execution. The domain was registered in October 2025. The incident is linked to previous attacks involving fake Python spell-checking tools and highlights the threat of slopsquatting, where AI agents hallucinate non-existent packages.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain: reconnaissance to identify PyPI as a target, weaponization by creating malicious packages, delivery through PyPI downloads, exploitation via package import, installation of the RAT, command and control through a C2 server, and actions on objectives including data exfiltration.

Title: Mustang Panda's Updated CoolClient Backdoor Targets Government Entities

diamond_model_summary: Mustang Panda, a Chinese espionage group, has updated its CoolClient backdoor to target government entities in Myanmar, Mongolia, Malaysia, Russia, and Pakistan. The malware is deployed via legitimate software from Sangfor and uses advanced techniques like clipboard monitoring and HTTP proxy credential sniffing. The group's strategic objective is to gather intelligence from government entities, employing TTPs such as DLL side-loading and persistence mechanisms like Registry modifications and new Windows services.
doc_summary: The Chinese espionage group Mustang Panda has updated its CoolClient backdoor, enhancing its capabilities to steal login data from browsers and monitor the clipboard. Kaspersky researchers have observed the malware being used to deploy a new rootkit, with a detailed technical analysis forthcoming. CoolClient, associated with Mustang Panda since 2022, is used alongside PlugX and LuminousMoth. The updated version targets government entities in Myanmar, Mongolia, Malaysia, Russia, and Pakistan, deployed via legitimate software from Sangfor. Previously, CoolClient was launched via DLL side-loading using signed binaries from Bitdefender, VLC Media Player, and Ulead PhotoImpact. The backdoor gathers system and user details, uses encrypted .DAT files for multi-stage execution, and achieves persistence through Registry modifications, new Windows services, and scheduled tasks. It supports UAC bypassing and privilege escalation. New features include clipboard monitoring, active window title tracking, and HTTP proxy credential sniffing. The plugin ecosystem now includes a remote shell plugin, a service management plugin, and a file management plugin. Infostealers target Chrome, Edge, and other Chromium-based browsers, using hardcoded API tokens for data exfiltration via Google Drive or Pixeldrain.
kill_chain_summary: The attack by Mustang Panda follows a structured kill chain. The delivery stage involves deploying the CoolClient malware via legitimate software from Sangfor. Installation is achieved through Registry modifications and new Windows services, ensuring persistence. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the vm2 JavaScript sandbox library, affecting versions up to 3.10.0, allows attackers to bypass sandbox protections and execute arbitrary code with full system privileges. The flaw, discovered by researcher patriksimek, exploits improper sanitization of Promise callback functions, enabling remote code execution without authentication or user interaction. The vm2 library, used in 273,000 npm projects, is designed to safely execute untrusted code in isolated environments. However, the vulnerability undermines this security guarantee through a Promise-based sandbox escape technique. Attackers can leverage async function return values to access unsanitized Promise.prototype.then callbacks, bypassing the intended sanitization layer. The flaw stems from inconsistent callback sanitization across Promise implementations, allowing attackers to exploit this inconsistency by constructing error objects with Symbol properties that trigger async function execution. This exposes the unsanitized globalPromise.prototype.then method, granting attackers access to the Error constructor’s Function prototype and enabling arbitrary code execution. The critical severity reflects full system compromise risks, and organizations must update vm2 to version 3.10.2 or later to mitigate the vulnerability.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploiting a vulnerability in the vm2 JavaScript sandbox library to achieve remote code execution. The exploitation stage is critical, as it allows attackers to bypass sandbox protections and execute arbitrary code with full system privileges. Title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Grist-Core (CVE-2026-24002)

Victim.Description: Users of Grist-Core, particularly those using the Pyodide sandboxing method, are at risk.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Grist-Core, allowing remote code execution through a Pyodide sandbox escape. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-24002, was discovered by Cyera Research Labs and affects users employing the Pyodide sandboxing method. The flaw enables malicious formulas to execute OS commands and JavaScript, compromising the host system. Grist has addressed the issue in version 1.7.9, recommending users update to mitigate risks.
doc_summary: A critical security flaw, CVE-2026-24002, known as Cellbreak, was disclosed in Grist-Core, an open-source spreadsheet-database. This vulnerability, discovered by Vladimir Tokarev of Cyera Research Labs, allows remote code execution (RCE) through a Pyodide sandbox escape. The flaw enables malicious formulas to execute OS commands or host-runtime JavaScript, compromising the boundary between cell logic and host execution. Grist addressed the issue in version 1.7.9 by moving Pyodide formula execution under the Deno JavaScript runtime. Users are advised to update to the latest version and set the GRIST_SANDBOX_FLAVOR environment variable to 'gvisor' to mitigate risks. The vulnerability highlights the need for capability-based sandboxing and defense-in-depth strategies.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves weaponization through malicious formulas exploiting the Pyodide sandbox escape in Grist-Core. Exploitation occurs when a user opens a malicious document, leading to command execution on the host. This allows attackers to perform actions on objectives, such as accessing sensitive data and executing commands, potentially leading to data breaches and lateral movement.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs involved in exploiting the Pyodide sandbox escape in Grist-Core. The vulnerability allows remote code execution, enabling attackers to execute OS commands and JavaScript. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains limits the ability to apply traditional detection methods, emphasizing the need for robust sandboxing and defense-in-depth strategies.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a JScript-based command-and-control framework called PeckBirdy, used by China-aligned APT actors since 2023. The framework targets Chinese gambling industries and Asian government entities, employing living-off-the-land binaries for execution. PeckBirdy serves fake software update pages to deliver malware, tracked as SHADOW-VOID-044. Another campaign, SHADOW-EARTH-045, targets Asian government entities, including a Philippine educational institution, for credential harvesting. doc_summary: The article discusses a new fake CAPTCHA scam that abuses Microsoft tools to install the Amatera Stealer malware. Discovered by Blackpoint Cyber, the attack uses legitimate Microsoft scripts and hides malicious code in Google Calendar and PNG images to bypass security measures and steal private passwords and browser data. The attack involves a fake CAPTCHA that tricks users into executing commands that initiate the infection process. The malware uses a Windows tool called SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs, a LOLBin, to evade detection. The attack is designed to avoid analysis by security sandboxes and uses steganography to hide malicious code in images. The final goal is to deliver Amatera Stealer, which targets saved passwords, credit card info, and browser data. The attack is effective on Windows 10, 11, or Server editions with App-V features enabled. Blackpoint Cyber advises against copying and pasting commands from websites into the Run box.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with a phishing email containing a fake CAPTCHA prompt, leading to the execution of commands that install the Amatera Stealer malware. The adversary uses steganography to hide malicious code in PNG files and employs a Windows tool called SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to evade detection. The malware communicates with C2 servers using HTTP/HTTPS and exfiltrates sensitive data such as passwords and credit card information. The attack is effective on Windows 10, 11, or Server editions with App-V features enabled, and the adversary's use of trusted infrastructure and sophisticated evasion techniques poses a significant threat.

doc_summary: ClearFake is a malware campaign that uses fake CAPTCHA challenges to trick users into installing malware. The malware also employs anti-analysis techniques to evade detection by security tools.

doc_summary: A newly discovered tool named Defendnot can disable Microsoft Defender on Windows systems by registering a fake antivirus product, even when no real antivirus is installed. This technique leverages an undocumented Windows Security Center (WSC) API, which is typically used by legitimate antivirus software to inform Windows that it is managing real-time protection. When such a product is registered, Windows automatically disables Microsoft Defender to prevent conflicts between multiple security applications. Defendnot, developed by security researcher es3n1n, exploits this behavior by registering a dummy antivirus product that passes all of Windows' validation checks. The tool is a successor to a previous project called no-defender, which was removed from GitHub following a DMCA takedown request due to the use of code from a third-party antivirus product. To avoid similar issues, Defendnot was built from scratch, using a dummy antivirus DLL. To bypass security measures, Defendnot injects its DLL into a trusted system process, such as Taskmgr.exe, which is signed and trusted by Microsoft. From within this process, it registers the fake antivirus with a spoofed display name. Once registered, Microsoft Defender immediately shuts itself off, leaving the system without active protection. The tool also includes a loader that allows configuration via a ctx.bin file, enabling users to set the antivirus name, toggle registration, and enable verbose logging. For persistence, Defendnot creates an autorun entry through the Windows Task Scheduler, ensuring it starts upon user login. Microsoft Defender currently detects and quarantines Defendnot as Win32/Sabsik.FL.!ml. This development underscores the importance of continuous monitoring and the need for robust security measures that can detect and prevent such sophisticated evasion techniques.
kill_chain_summary: The Defendnot incident involves several stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Weaponization is achieved through the development of a dummy antivirus DLL. Exploitation occurs by leveraging an undocumented API to disable Microsoft Defender. Installation involves DLL injection into trusted processes. Actions on objectives are realized by impairing defenses, leaving systems unprotected. Detection and remediation focus on monitoring API calls, DLL injections, and antivirus status changes, alongside implementing secure development practices and additional security layers.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Defendnot tool presents a significant challenge on the Pyramid of Pain. The use of a unique tool (Defendnot) and specific TTPs (fake antivirus registration, DLL injection) makes detection and response difficult. While no specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, the focus on tools and TTPs highlights the sophistication of the attack. Effective detection requires monitoring API calls and DLL injections, while remediation involves applying patches and enhancing security monitoring.

Title: Amatera Infostealer Delivered via ClickFix and App-V Script

Victim.Description: The campaign targets users who can be tricked into executing commands via the Windows Run dialog.

diamond_model_summary: The Amatera infostealer campaign demonstrates a high level of sophistication by leveraging trusted Microsoft components and steganography to evade detection. The adversary employs the ClickFix method to trick users into executing malicious commands, ultimately delivering the Amatera malware. The infrastructure includes the use of public Google Calendar for configuration data and public CDNs for payload delivery. The campaign targets users who can be tricked into executing commands via the Windows Run dialog, with the primary objective of data theft and credential harvesting.
doc_summary: A new malicious campaign has been identified that combines the ClickFix method with fake CAPTCHA and a signed Microsoft Application Virtualization (App-V) script to deliver the Amatera infostealing malware. The App-V script acts as a living-off-the-land binary, proxying PowerShell execution through a trusted Microsoft component. The attack begins with a fake CAPTCHA check, leading victims to execute a command via the Windows Run dialog. This command abuses the legitimate SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs script to launch PowerShell. The malware retrieves configuration data from a public Google Calendar file and uses steganography to hide payloads in PNG images. The final stage involves decrypting and executing the Amatera infostealer, which connects to a hardcoded IP address for further payloads. BlackPoint Cyber classifies Amatera as a standard infostealer, with its operators using the ClickFix method for delivery. Recommendations include restricting Windows Run dialog access, removing unnecessary App-V components, enabling PowerShell logging, and monitoring outbound connections.
kill_chain_summary: The Amatera infostealer campaign follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the delivery of a fake CAPTCHA to trick users into executing a command via the Windows Run dialog. The weaponization stage involves the use of a signed Microsoft App-V script to proxy PowerShell execution. The exploitation stage sees the execution of the App-V script to launch PowerShell, while the installation stage involves retrieving and executing the Amatera infostealer. Command and control is established through a hardcoded IP address, and the final stage involves the collection of browser data and credentials.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Amatera infostealer campaign presents several challenges for defenders, as it employs trusted Microsoft components and steganography to evade detection. The use of living-off-the-land binaries and steganography makes it difficult to detect and block the malware. The campaign's reliance on public infrastructure, such as Google Calendar and public CDNs, further complicates detection efforts. The lack of specific indicators, such as hashes or IP addresses, makes it challenging to apply traditional detection methods, highlighting the need for advanced threat hunting and detection capabilities.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-24061 in GNU InetUtils Telnetd Server

Victim.Description: IoT devices and legacy systems running vulnerable versions of GNU InetUtils telnetd.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves attackers exploiting CVE-2026-24061, a critical vulnerability in the GNU InetUtils telnetd server, to gain unauthorized root access. The adversary's capability includes crafting a malicious USER environment variable to bypass authentication. The infrastructure is characterized by a large number of exposed Telnet services globally, particularly in Asia, South America, and Europe. Victims are primarily IoT devices and legacy systems running vulnerable software versions.
doc_summary: Internet security watchdog Shadowserver tracks nearly 800,000 IP addresses with Telnet fingerprints amid ongoing attacks exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the GNU InetUtils telnetd server. The security flaw (CVE-2026-24061) impacts GNU InetUtils versions 1.9.3 through 2.7 and was patched in version 2.8. The telnetd server invokes /usr/bin/login passing the value of the USER environment variable received from the client as the last parameter. If the client supplies a carefully crafted USER environment value being the string '-f root', and passes the telnet(1) -a or --login parameter to send this USER environment to the server, the client will be automatically logged in as root bypassing normal authentication processes. Shadowserver is tracking over 380,000 from Asia, almost 170,000 from South America, and just over 100,000 from Europe. There is no information regarding how many of these devices have been secured against CVE-2026-24061 attacks. The malicious activity started on January 21 and originated from 18 IP addresses across 60 Telnet sessions, abusing the Telnet IAC option negotiation to inject 'USER=-f <user>' and grant attackers' shell access to compromised devices without authentication. Admins who can't immediately upgrade their devices to the patched release are advised to disable the vulnerable telnetd service or block TCP port 23 on all firewalls.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify exposed Telnet services. Weaponization involves crafting a malicious USER environment variable. Delivery occurs via Telnet, exploiting CVE-2026-24061 to gain root access. Post-exploitation, attackers attempt to install Python malware and establish command and control through Telnet sessions. Actions on objectives include further reconnaissance and potential lateral movement.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses used in the attack, the specific CVE-2026-24061 vulnerability, and the Telnet protocol as a tool. The exploitation of this vulnerability represents a significant challenge for defenders, as it requires patching vulnerable systems and monitoring for unauthorized Telnet activity. The presence of Python malware attempts further complicates detection and response efforts.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a BGP route leak caused by a policy misconfiguration at Cloudflare, affecting IPv6 traffic. doc_summary: Cloudflare experienced a BGP route leak incident on January 22, 2023, affecting IPv6 traffic and causing congestion, packet loss, and approximately 12 Gbps of dropped traffic. The incident was due to a policy misconfiguration on a router, leading to the redistribution of routes in Miami. This resulted in a mixture of Type 3 and Type 4 route leaks as defined in RFC7908. The leak caused traffic to be sent through unintended networks, violating valley-free rules and leading to dropped traffic. Cloudflare quickly detected the issue, manually reverted the configuration, and paused automation to mitigate the impact within 25 minutes. Measures to prevent future occurrences include stricter export safeguards, CI/CD checks, improved detection, and promoting RPKI ASPA adoption.
kill_chain_summary: The BGP route leak incident did not follow a traditional cyber kill chain as it was not a deliberate attack. The misconfiguration led to unintended route advertisements, causing network congestion and packet loss. Cloudflare's response involved quick detection and manual configuration rollback to mitigate the impact.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The BGP route leak incident did not involve specific indicators like hashes, IPs, or domains typically used in the Pyramid of Pain. Title: MaliciousCorgi: Malicious VS Code Extensions Exfiltrating Developer Data

Victim.Description: Developers using Visual Studio Code extensions are targeted, with their data being exfiltrated without consent.

diamond_model_summary: The MaliciousCorgi campaign involves adversaries using malicious Visual Studio Code extensions to exfiltrate developer data to China-based servers. The extensions, disguised as AI-powered coding assistants, function as advertised while covertly capturing and exfiltrating data. The adversary's infrastructure includes servers in China and analytics SDKs for device fingerprinting. The campaign targets developers globally, posing a high risk due to the widespread use of Visual Studio Code.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered two malicious Microsoft Visual Studio Code extensions, advertised as AI-powered coding assistants, that exfiltrate developer data to China-based servers. The extensions, with 1.5 million installs, capture file modifications and send them to aihao123.cn. The campaign, named MaliciousCorgi, uses identical spyware infrastructure under different publisher names. The extensions function as advertised, providing autocomplete suggestions and error explanations, while covertly reading file contents, encoding them in Base64, and exfiltrating them. A hidden zero-pixel iframe loads four Chinese analytics SDKs for device fingerprinting. The disclosure coincides with the identification of six zero-day vulnerabilities in JavaScript package managers, collectively named PackageGate. These vulnerabilities allow bypassing security controls in npm, pnpm, vlt, and Bun. GitHub is addressing the issue, urging the adoption of trusted publishing and 2FA. The incident highlights the risks of supply chain attacks and the need for robust security measures.
kill_chain_summary: The MaliciousCorgi campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify popular VS Code extensions. The adversary weaponizes these extensions with malicious code, delivering them through the Visual Studio Marketplace. Once installed, the extensions exploit their legitimate functionality to exfiltrate data to a C2 server in China. The campaign includes command and control communication and actions on objectives, such as data exfiltration and device fingerprinting using analytics SDKs.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the MaliciousCorgi campaign includes domain names like aihao123.cn, which are critical for the adversary's operations. The use of legitimate Visual Studio Code extensions as tools makes detection challenging. The campaign's TTPs involve data exfiltration and device fingerprinting, posing significant challenges for defenders. The adversary's infrastructure and techniques highlight the need for robust detection and remediation strategies.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a cyber espionage campaign targeting Indian users. Title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server Actively Exploited

Victim.Description: Organizations using VMware vCenter Server, particularly federal agencies.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical RCE vulnerability, CVE-2024-37079, in VMware vCenter Server, actively exploited by threat actors. The adversary's capability includes exploiting an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the DCERPC protocol, potentially leading to full control over virtual machines. The infrastructure targeted is VMware vCenter Server instances, with victims primarily being organizations using this software, especially within the United States government sector.
doc_summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has identified a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2024-37079, in Broadcom VMware vCenter Server. This vulnerability, an out-of-bounds write affecting the DCERPC protocol, allows threat actors to execute arbitrary code without authentication. CISA has added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, indicating active exploitation. Federal agencies are mandated to patch systems by February 13, 2026, under Binding Operational Directive 22-01. The flaw poses a high risk for initial access to enterprise virtualization infrastructure, potentially leading to full control over virtual machines and sensitive workloads. Organizations are urged to apply vendor mitigations or implement network segmentation if patches are unavailable.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation of a public-facing application vulnerability (CVE-2024-37079) in VMware vCenter Server. The exploitation stage is critical, allowing threat actors to achieve remote code execution without authentication. This can lead to actions on objectives, such as gaining full control over virtual machines and sensitive workloads. Detection involves monitoring DCERPC traffic and unauthorized network connections, while remediation includes applying vendor mitigations and network segmentation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs, as the exploitation of CVE-2024-37079 is a significant tactic used by threat actors. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, but the use of the DCERPC protocol and the targeting of VMware vCenter Server are key indicators. The scoring reflects the emphasis on TTPs, which are challenging for adversaries to change.

Victim.Description: Organizations using Apache Hadoop HDFS native client versions 3.2.0 through 3.4.1.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in Apache Hadoop's HDFS native client, specifically an out-of-bounds write in the URI parser. This vulnerability, CVE-2025-27821, affects versions 3.2.0 through 3.4.1 and can lead to system crashes or data corruption. The adversary could exploit this by providing malicious URIs, impacting organizations using HDFS for sensitive data storage.
doc_summary: A moderate out-of-bounds write vulnerability identified as CVE-2025-27821 affects Apache Hadoop's HDFS native client, specifically the URI parser. Discovered by security researcher BUI Ngoc Tan, this flaw allows untrusted input to write data beyond allocated memory boundaries, potentially leading to system crashes, data corruption, or denial-of-service conditions. The vulnerability impacts versions 3.2.0 through 3.4.1 of the HDFS native client, with version 3.4.2 and later unaffected. Apache recommends immediate upgrades to version 3.4.2 to mitigate risks. The issue is tracked under JIRA ticket HDFS-17754. Organizations using HDFS for sensitive data storage are at particular risk, and system administrators should monitor logs for suspicious URI patterns and implement network-level access controls.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of a vulnerability in the URI parser of Apache Hadoop's HDFS native client. The adversary can exploit this vulnerability to execute code, leading to potential memory corruption and denial-of-service conditions. Organizations are advised to upgrade to version 3.4.2 and monitor logs for suspicious activity.

Title: CVE-2026-24061 Exploit in GNU Inetutils Telnetd

Victim.Description: Systems running vulnerable versions of GNU Inetutils telnetd.
Victim.Security_Posture: Legacy systems with exposed telnet services.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-24061, a critical vulnerability in GNU Inetutils telnetd, allowing remote code execution. The adversary is likely opportunistic, exploiting exposed telnet services globally. The infrastructure includes over 800,000 vulnerable telnet instances, making it a significant target for mass-exploitation campaigns. Victims are systems running legacy telnet services, with a critical impact severity due to the potential for credential harvesting and lateral movement.
doc_summary: A proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-24061, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in the GNU Inetutils telnetd, has surfaced. Security researchers warn that over 800,000 vulnerable instances remain publicly accessible on the internet. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on affected systems running vulnerable versions of the telnetd service. CVE-2026-24061 affects GNU InetUtils telnetd, a legacy remote login service that provides unencrypted terminal access over the network. The vulnerability stems from improper input validation in the telnet daemon, allowing attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms and execute arbitrary commands on target systems. With the release of working proof-of-concept code, exploitation is now trivial for threat actors with minimal technical expertise. The Shadowserver Foundation’s Accessible Telnet Report reveals the scale of the problem. Approximately 800,000 telnet instances remain exposed on port 23/TCP across the internet, presenting an attractive target surface for mass-exploitation campaigns. Organizations should immediately audit their network perimeter for exposed Telnet services on port 23/TCP and alternative ports (2323, 2222). Priority remediation involves disabling telnetd entirely, migrating to SSH, or implementing strict firewall rules limiting telnet access to trusted internal networks only. Security teams should monitor threat intelligence feeds for exploit activity targeting this vulnerability.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where adversaries scan for exposed telnet services on port 23/TCP. Weaponization involves the development of a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-24061. Exploitation occurs when attackers use this exploit to execute arbitrary commands on vulnerable systems. Actions on objectives include credential harvesting and lateral movement. The incident highlights the need for immediate remediation, such as disabling telnet services and migrating to SSH.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs associated with exploiting CVE-2026-24061. While specific IP addresses, domains, or hash values are not identified, the widespread exposure of telnet services and the availability of a proof-of-concept exploit make this a critical threat. Organizations should focus on mitigating the vulnerability by disabling telnet services and monitoring for unusual activity.

doc_summary: In November 2025, Anthropic reported the first known AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign, featuring AI throughout the attack stages. Google's Threat Intelligence Group noted adversaries using Large Language Models to conceal code and generate malicious scripts. ClickFix-related attacks used steganography to hide malware in images, bypassing signature-based scans. Octo Tempest exploited AV exclusion rules via social engineering and SIM swapping. Blockade Spider used mixed domains for ransomware, while Volt Typhoon used living off the land techniques to evade detection. NDR and EDR systems are essential to detect AI-fueled threats.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with AI-driven reconnaissance to gather intelligence on targets. Weaponization involved AI-generated scripts and steganography to prepare payloads. Delivery was achieved through social engineering and steganography. Exploitation involved AV exclusion rule manipulation. Installation saw malware deployed on compromised systems. Command and control were established via AI-driven communication. Actions on objectives included data exfiltration and intelligence gathering.

The infrastructure involves improperly secured WordPress sites for malware distribution and command-and-control. doc_summary: The North Korean threat actor Konni, also known as Earth Imp, Opal Sleet, Osmium, TA406, and Vedalia, has been observed using AI-generated PowerShell malware to target developers and engineering teams in the blockchain sector. The campaign, named Operation Poseidon, has expanded its reach to Japan, Australia, and India, beyond its usual targets in South Korea, Russia, Ukraine, and European nations. The attacks involve spear-phishing emails with malicious links disguised as advertising URLs to bypass security filters, delivering the EndRAT malware. The campaign uses improperly secured WordPress sites for malware distribution and command-and-control infrastructure. The PowerShell backdoor's modular structure and human-readable documentation suggest AI assistance in its creation. The campaign aims to establish a foothold in development environments for broader access across multiple projects and services.
kill_chain_summary: Operation Poseidon by the Konni threat actor follows a structured kill chain. The campaign begins with spear-phishing emails containing malicious links disguised as advertising URLs. The weaponization stage involves AI-generated PowerShell malware. Delivery is achieved through spear-phishing, leading to the installation of EndRAT malware. Command and control are maintained via WordPress sites, and the ultimate objective is to establish a foothold in development environments for broader access.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for Operation Poseidon includes several indicators. Domain names such as ad.doubleclick.net are used for ad click redirection. The campaign employs AI-generated PowerShell malware and the EndRAT malware family. The use of improperly secured WordPress sites for command-and-control infrastructure is a key network host artifact. These indicators provide opportunities for detection and response to disrupt the adversary's operations.

Title: ShinyHunters Voice Phishing Attack on SSO Platforms

Victim.Description: Companies using SSO services from Okta, Microsoft, and Google.

diamond_model_summary: The ShinyHunters group has been identified as the adversary behind a series of voice phishing attacks targeting SSO platforms. Their capability includes the use of sophisticated phishing kits that allow real-time interaction with victims. The infrastructure involves phishing sites mimicking legitimate company portals. Victims are primarily companies in the technology sector using SSO services, with a high impact severity due to the potential access to multiple connected applications.
doc_summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang is behind a series of voice phishing attacks targeting single sign-on (SSO) accounts at Okta, Microsoft, and Google. These attacks involve threat actors impersonating IT support to trick employees into entering credentials and multi-factor authentication codes on phishing sites. Once compromised, attackers gain access to SSO accounts, providing entry to connected enterprise applications like Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and Google Workspace. The group has issued extortion demands to multiple companies, confirming their involvement. ShinyHunters uses data from previous breaches to enhance social engineering efforts. The phishing kits employed allow real-time interaction with victims, guiding them through the login process. Despite denials from Microsoft and Google about product abuse, ShinyHunters claims responsibility for the attacks, with Salesforce as a primary target.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance using data from previous breaches to identify targets. Weaponization involves creating phishing kits to mimic SSO login portals. Delivery is executed through voice phishing calls to employees. Exploitation occurs when victims enter credentials on phishing sites. Actions on objectives include harvesting data from compromised SSO accounts. The attack leverages social engineering and phishing techniques to gain initial access and exploit SSO vulnerabilities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names used in phishing sites, which are relatively easy for defenders to change and block. The tools used, such as phishing kits, are more challenging to counter as they require understanding and dismantling the attack infrastructure. The TTPs employed, including social engineering and phishing, are the most difficult to change as they rely on human behavior and require comprehensive training and awareness programs to mitigate.

Title: Exploitation of GNU InetUtils Telnetd Authentication Bypass Vulnerability

Victim.Description: Internet-exposed systems running vulnerable versions of GNU InetUtils telnetd.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in GNU InetUtils telnetd, allowing remote attackers to gain root access without authentication. The adversary's capability includes leveraging publicly available proof-of-concept code to exploit the vulnerability. The infrastructure used includes IP addresses for exploitation and malware distribution. Victims are internet-exposed systems running vulnerable versions of GNU InetUtils telnetd.
doc_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in GNU InetUtils telnetd, affecting versions 1.9.3 through 2.7. The flaw allows remote attackers to gain root access without authentication by manipulating the USER environment variable. The vulnerability was discovered by Kyu Neushwaistein and reported on January 19, 2026, with an advisory published by Simon Josefsson on January 20, 2026. GreyNoise Labs detected 18 unique attacker IP addresses conducting 60 exploitation attempts over an 18-hour period. The most prolific attacker, originating from IP 178.16.53.82, launched 12 sessions targeting 10 systems. Network traffic analysis revealed all captured packets were Telnet protocol communications on TCP port 23. Intrusion detection systems confirmed successful root-level access by some attackers. The malware distribution server at IP 67.220.95.16 was observed serving a Python payload, likely a botnet client or cryptomining malware.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable systems, followed by weaponization and delivery of crafted payloads via the Telnet protocol. Exploitation occurs through an authentication bypass vulnerability, potentially leading to installation of malware and command and control communication. Actions on objectives may include further reconnaissance and deployment of additional payloads.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses used for exploitation and malware distribution, as well as the tools and techniques employed by the adversary. The exploitation of the authentication bypass vulnerability in GNU InetUtils telnetd is a key TTP. Monitoring and blocking these indicators can significantly disrupt the adversary's operations.

Title: AI Agents and Access Drift in Enterprise Environments

Victim.Description: Enterprises using AI agents for productivity

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves AI agents in enterprise environments, which are granted broad access permissions and operate autonomously. These agents differ from traditional users and service accounts, leading to access drift and potential security risks. The lack of clear ownership and accountability for these agents exacerbates the risk, as they can perform actions beyond user permissions. The incident highlights the need for redefining risk management and establishing clear ownership and accountability for AI agents.
doc_summary: AI agents are transforming enterprise productivity by automating tasks such as scheduling, data access, and workflow management. However, they introduce significant security challenges due to their broad access permissions and lack of clear ownership. Unlike traditional users or service accounts, AI agents operate autonomously and persistently, often acting on behalf of multiple users across systems. This can lead to access drift, where agents accumulate permissions over time without proper oversight. The risk varies based on the type of agent, with organizational agents posing the highest risk due to their broad, persistent permissions and lack of accountability. Securing AI agents requires redefining risk management, establishing clear ownership, and mapping user-agent interactions to prevent unauthorized access and mitigate potential security breaches.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves AI agents exploiting their broad access permissions to perform unauthorized actions. These agents operate autonomously across systems, acting as access intermediaries and potentially enabling unauthorized access to sensitive data. The lack of clear ownership and accountability for these agents increases the risk of unauthorized actions and security breaches. The incident underscores the need for visibility into user-agent interactions and mapping agent access to prevent unauthorized access and mitigate potential security risks.

Title: TrustAsia SSL/TLS Certificate Revocation Due to ACME Service Vulnerability

Victim.Description: Organizations using TrustAsia's LiteSSL ACME service

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a critical vulnerability in TrustAsia's LiteSSL ACME service, allowing unauthorized certificate issuance. The adversary exploited a logic error in domain validation, impacting organizations using the service. TrustAsia's rapid response included revoking affected certificates and patching the vulnerability.
doc_summary: TrustAsia revoked 143 SSL/TLS certificates after discovering a critical vulnerability in its LiteSSL ACME service. The flaw allowed unauthorized certificate issuance by reusing domain validation data across different ACME accounts, violating CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements. The issue was due to a logic error in handling Authorization objects, failing to verify if a CSR originated from the same ACME account that performed the initial validation. Attackers could hijack the issuance process and obtain wildcard certificates without re-triggering DNS-01 challenges. TrustAsia suspended ACME issuance services, deployed patches, and revoked affected certificates. The incident highlights the importance of proper account context validation in ACME implementations.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident primarily involved the exploitation stage, where attackers leveraged a vulnerability in the LiteSSL ACME service to issue unauthorized certificates. TrustAsia's response included suspending services, deploying patches, and revoking certificates, effectively mitigating the threat within hours.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the domain validation process and the ACME service vulnerability. No specific hashes, IPs, or tools were identified, but the exploitation of the ACME protocol and domain validation logic error are key TTPs. TrustAsia's remediation efforts addressed these vulnerabilities.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a dual-vector campaign exploiting stolen credentials to deploy Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software for persistent access. The attack involves phishing emails disguised as Greenvelope invitations to harvest credentials for Microsoft Outlook, Yahoo!, and AOL.com. Compromised emails are used to register with LogMeIn, generating RMM access tokens. These tokens are deployed via an executable named 'GreenVelopeCard.exe', signed with a valid certificate, to install LogMeIn Resolve. The RMM tool is used to alter service settings for unrestricted access and establish hidden scheduled tasks. Organizations are advised to monitor unauthorized RMM installations.

Finally, actions on objectives include maintaining persistent access and control over victim systems.

Microsoft emphasizes the need for revoking active session cookies and removing attacker-created rules. Title: Critical Code Injection Vulnerability in Node.js binary-parser Library

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical code injection vulnerability in the Node.js binary-parser library, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript code. The vulnerability affects versions before 2.3.0 and is due to unsafe dynamic code generation. Attackers can exploit this flaw by injecting malicious payloads into field names or encoding parameters, leading to full process compromise. The flaw is particularly dangerous in server environments, where attackers can gain shell access, steal sensitive data, or pivot to other systems. doc_summary: A critical code injection vulnerability in the Node.js binary-parser library exposes applications to arbitrary JavaScript execution. CERT/CC published Vulnerability Note VU#102648 on January 20, 2026, assigning it CVE-2026-1245. The flaw affects versions before 2.3.0 and stems from unsafe dynamic code generation. Developers using untrusted input for parser definitions face severe risks, including full process compromise. The vulnerability arises during parser instantiation, allowing attackers to inject malicious payloads into field names or encoding parameters. This prototype pollution-style flaw leaves no network signatures or file artifacts. Detection relies on behavioral monitoring. Upgrade to binary-parser 2.3.0 or later to mitigate the risk. Researchers Maor Caplan reported the issue, and Timur Snoke authored the CERT note.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of the Node.js binary-parser library through code injection. Attackers can inject malicious payloads into field names or encoding parameters, leading to arbitrary JavaScript execution. doc_summary: Hasan Gürsoy reported a cybersecurity incident involving a part-time developer job scam on LinkedIn. The scam involved a take-home assignment containing sophisticated backdoor code with Remote Code Execution (RCE) capabilities. The malicious code fetched arbitrary JavaScript from a remote server, executed it with full system access, and used base64 encoding to hide suspicious environment variables. It had access to require(), leading to a complete Node.js system compromise. Potential impacts included credential theft, database access, and malware installation. Red flags included unsolicited LinkedIn messages, simple assignments, and obfuscated code. Gürsoy advised reviewing code before execution, using isolated environments, and researching companies thoroughly. The incident highlights the importance of vigilance against fake job offers, especially those related to NFT real estate projects like 'Golden City'.

Weaponization involves creating malicious code disguised as a take-home assignment. Delivery occurs through LinkedIn messages, leading to exploitation via JavaScript execution. diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a malicious package 'sympy-dev' on PyPI, impersonating the SymPy library to deploy a cryptocurrency miner on Linux hosts. The adversary uses a backdoored package to execute a downloader for an XMRig miner, triggered by specific polynomial routines. The infrastructure includes a remote server at IP 63.250.56.54, hosting the JSON configuration and ELF payload. The attack targets developers and users of PyPI, exploiting the trust in the platform to gain initial access and execute malicious code.
doc_summary: A malicious package named 'sympy-dev' was discovered in the Python Package Index (PyPI), impersonating the popular SymPy library to deploy a cryptocurrency miner on Linux hosts. The package mimics SymPy's project description to deceive users into downloading it as a development version. Since its publication on January 17, 2026, it has been downloaded over 1,100 times. The package acts as a downloader for an XMRig cryptocurrency miner, triggered by specific polynomial routines. It retrieves a remote JSON configuration and an ELF payload from IP address 63.250.56.54, executing it in memory to avoid disk artifacts. The attack aims to mine cryptocurrency using XMRig, with configurations disabling GPU backends and directing the miner to Stratum over TLS endpoints. The Python implant functions as a general-purpose loader for arbitrary second-stage code execution.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify a popular library to impersonate, followed by weaponization through the creation of a malicious package. Delivery occurs via PyPI, where users download the package, leading to exploitation as the package executes on victim systems. Installation involves deploying a cryptocurrency miner, with command and control established through communication with a remote server. The final stage, actions on objectives, sees the miner using system resources to mine cryptocurrency.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes an IP address (63.250.56.54) used for command and control, and the tool XMRig for cryptocurrency mining. Title: CyberSCI Nationals 2021: Command and Control Track Analysis

Victim.Description: Victims are globally distributed computers controlled by the C2 server.
Victim.Industry: Various, as the victims are not industry-specific

diamond_model_summary: The diamond model analysis reveals that the adversary, dogedays, is engaged in cryptomining and ransomware operations using a C2 server infrastructure. Their capabilities include exploiting Apache Druid vulnerabilities and maintaining persistence through SSH key installation. The victims are globally distributed computers, and the adversary's motivation is financial gain. The infrastructure involves a C2 server at c2-server.dogedays.ca, with IP address ip-10-0-1-35, using TCP/IP for communication. The adversary employs tools like Metasploit and uncompyle6 to achieve their objectives.
doc_summary: The document details the author's participation in the CyberSCI Nationals 2021, focusing on the Command and Control track. The scenario involves a group called dogedays, involved in cryptomining and ransomware, with the task of breaking into their operations. The challenges include obtaining access to a C2 server and shutting down malware on victim machines. The author describes using an Apache Druid 0.20.0 Remote Command Execution exploit via Metasploit to gain access, and then decompiling Python bytecode with uncompyle6 to understand the C2 server's functionality. The process involves implementing RSA signature verification to successfully shut down the malware. The document serves as a detailed walkthrough of the challenges faced and solutions implemented during the competition.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain analysis identifies several stages in the incident. Reconnaissance involved scanning the C2 server for open ports and services. Weaponization was achieved through exploiting Apache Druid vulnerabilities using Metasploit. Exploitation involved gaining shell access to the C2 server. Installation was achieved by adding SSH keys for persistence. Command and Control was established through the C2 server, allowing control over victim machines. Actions on Objectives involved shutting down malware on victim machines. Each stage involved specific tactics and techniques, with corresponding detection and remediation strategies.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The pyramid of pain analysis identifies several indicators of compromise. Hash values and IP addresses were not specifically mentioned, but the domain name dogedays.ca and IP address ip-10-0-1-35 were identified. Network host artifacts include the C2 server and victim machines. Tools used include Metasploit and uncompyle6, while TTPs involve exploiting Apache Druid vulnerabilities and maintaining persistence through SSH key installation. The analysis highlights the importance of monitoring these indicators to detect and respond to similar incidents.

Title: Unauthorized Firewall Configuration Changes on Fortinet FortiGate Devices

Victim.Description: Fortinet FortiGate devices are targeted, impacting organizations using these devices.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to unpatched SSO feature

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary exploiting Fortinet vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access to FortiGate devices. The adversary uses automated techniques to create persistence accounts and exfiltrate firewall configurations. The infrastructure includes multiple IP addresses used for malicious SSO logins. The victims are organizations using Fortinet FortiGate devices, with a high impact severity due to the potential for data exfiltration.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity company Arctic Wolf has identified a new cluster of automated malicious activity targeting Fortinet FortiGate devices. The activity began on January 15, 2026, and is similar to a December 2025 campaign involving malicious SSO logins exploiting CVE-2025-59718 and CVE-2025-59719. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated bypass of SSO login authentication via crafted SAML messages when the FortiCloud SSO feature is enabled. The attack involves creating generic accounts for persistence, making unauthorized firewall configuration changes, and exfiltrating configuration files. Malicious logins were recorded from four different IP addresses, and secondary accounts such as 'secadmin' and 'itadmin' were created. The activity is automated, occurring within seconds. Users reported similar issues on Reddit, and Fortinet has been contacted for comment. Disabling the 'admin-forticloud-sso-login' setting is advised.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of Fortinet vulnerabilities for unauthorized SSO logins, followed by the creation of persistence accounts. The adversary then exfiltrates firewall configuration files, indicating a well-coordinated attack. The exploitation stage is critical, leveraging known CVEs to bypass authentication. The installation stage involves creating secondary accounts for persistence, while the actions on objectives stage focuses on data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses used for malicious logins and the exploitation of specific CVEs. The adversary's use of generic accounts for persistence and the exfiltration of configuration files are key indicators. The scoring reflects the presence of multiple IP addresses and the exploitation of known vulnerabilities, highlighting the adversary's capability to conduct automated attacks.

Title: Cisco Patches Critical Zero-Day Vulnerability CVE-2026-20045

Victim.Description: Organizations using affected Cisco products

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-20045, affecting Cisco's Unified Communications products. The adversary exploits this vulnerability to execute arbitrary commands and escalate privileges to root. Cisco has released patches to mitigate the risk, and CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The infrastructure and specific adversary details remain unidentified.
doc_summary: Cisco has released patches for a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-20045, affecting Unified Communications products and Webex Calling Dedicated Instance. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands and escalate privileges to root. The vulnerability, due to improper validation of user-supplied input in HTTP requests, has been actively exploited in the wild. Cisco urges customers to upgrade to a fixed software release, as no workarounds are available. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added CVE-2026-20045 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to apply fixes by February 11, 2026. This incident follows another critical vulnerability, CVE-2025-20393, affecting Cisco Secure Email Gateway.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-20045, in Cisco's Unified Communications products. The adversary gains initial access by sending crafted HTTP requests, leading to arbitrary command execution and potential privilege escalation to root. Cisco has released patches to address the vulnerability, and organizations are urged to apply these updates promptly.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-20045, which is a significant challenge to detect and remediate. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains have been identified, making detection reliant on monitoring HTTP request patterns and unauthorized command execution. The release of patches by Cisco is a critical step in mitigating the threat.

Victim.Description: LastPass users targeted by phishing emails.

diamond_model_summary: The LastPass phishing campaign is characterized by an adversary using social engineering tactics to deceive users into revealing their vault master passwords. The adversary's capability involves crafting convincing phishing emails and setting up a fake domain to capture credentials. The infrastructure includes phishing domains and email addresses, while the victims are LastPass users, primarily in the United States. The campaign's objective is to gain unauthorized access to user credentials for financial gain.
doc_summary: LastPass warns of a phishing campaign disguised as a maintenance notification, urging users to back up their vaults within 24 hours. The emails, sent from addresses like support@lastpass.server8 and support@sr22vegas.com, redirect users to a phishing site at mail-lastpass.com. The campaign began on January 19, targeting users during a holiday weekend in the United States. LastPass emphasizes it never asks for master passwords and advises reporting incidents to abuse@lastpass.com. The phishing emails exploit social engineering tactics to create urgency, aiming to steal vault master passwords.
kill_chain_summary: The LastPass phishing campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to gather email addresses of LastPass users. The weaponization phase involves crafting phishing emails that mimic legitimate LastPass communications. Delivery is executed through sending these emails to users, who are then exploited by clicking on links that redirect them to a phishing site. The adversary's ultimate goal is to perform actions on objectives by stealing vault master passwords, although no significant installation or command and control activities are detected.
